text: Would that you were a brother to me,nursed at my mother's breasts!If I met you out of doors, I would kiss youand none would despise me.
t[AA] I would lead you, bring you to my mother's house,where you would teach me,Where I would give you to drinkspiced wine, my pomegranate [1] juice.
t[AB] His left hand is under my head,and his right arm embraces me.
t[AC] I adjure you, Daughters of Jerusalem,do not awaken or stir up loveuntil it is ready!
D? [AD] Who is this coming up from the desert,leaning upon her lover?W Beneath the apple tree I awakened you; [2]there your mother conceived you;there she who bore you conceived.
Set me as a seal [3] upon your heart,as a seal upon your arm;For Love is strong as Death,longing is fierce as Sheol.Its arrows are arrows of fire,flames of the divine.
t[AE] Deep waters [4] cannot quench love,nor rivers sweep it away.Were one to offer all the wealth of his house for love,he would be utterly despised.
W "We have a little sister; [5]she has no breasts as yet.What shall we do for our sisteron the day she is spoken for?
If she is a wall,we will build upon her a silver turret;But if she is a door,we will board her up with cedar planks."
I am a wall, [6]and my breasts are like towers.I became in his eyesas one who brings peace.
M? Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon; [7]he gave over the vineyard to caretakers.For its fruit one would have to paya thousand silver pieces.
My vineyard is at my own disposal;the thousand pieces are for you, Solomon,and two hundred for the caretakers of its fruit.
M You who dwell in the gardens, [8]my companions are listening for your voice—let me hear it!
W [AF] Swiftly, my lover,be like a gazelle or a young stagupon the mountains of spices.
